\section[a origem]{a origem — the origin}

\label{lesson:PT-C350-origem}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for consequently, then the Portuguese for due to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a origem}
\textbf{a origem} — \textquotedblleft{}the origin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ninguém sabe a origem desta tradição.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nobody knows the origin of this tradition.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ter origem em} — to originate in. \emph{De origem portuguesa} — of Portuguese origin.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{origem} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{orīgō, orīginis} \textquotedblleft{}beginning, source, descent\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{orīrī} \textquotedblleft{}to rise, to arise\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a origem}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a origem}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a origem}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for consequently, then the Portuguese for due to, then say \emph{a origem} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a origem mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The origin\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[derivar]{derivar — to derive, to come from}

\label{lesson:PT-C350-derivar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for due to, then the Portuguese for the origin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: derivar}
\textbf{derivar} — \textquotedblleft{}to derive, to come from\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Muitas palavras portuguesas derivam do latim.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Many Portuguese words come from Latin.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Derivar de} — to come from.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{derivar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dērīvāre} \textquotedblleft{}to lead or draw off a liquid\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{dē} and \emph{rīvus} \textquotedblleft{}a stream\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{derivar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{derivar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{derivar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for due to, then the Portuguese for the origin, then say \emph{derivar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does derivar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To derive, to come from\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[resultar]{resultar — to result; to work out}

\label{lesson:PT-C350-resultar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the origin, then the Portuguese for to derive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: resultar}
\textbf{resultar} — \textquotedblleft{}to result; to work out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O acidente resultou de um erro do motorista.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The accident resulted from the driver's mistake.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Resultar de} — to result from; \emph{resultar em} — to lead to. Also to work: \emph{o plano resultou}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{resultar} comes from Medieval Latin \emph{resultāre} (EtymDB), Latin \emph{resultāre} \textquotedblleft{}to spring or leap back, to rebound\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{saltāre} \textquotedblleft{}to jump\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{resultar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{resultar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{resultar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the origin, then the Portuguese for to derive, then say \emph{resultar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does resultar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To result; to work out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[originar]{originar — to give rise to, to cause}

\label{lesson:PT-C350-originar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to derive, then the Portuguese for to result.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: originar}
\textbf{originar} — \textquotedblleft{}to give rise to, to cause\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A tempestade originou cortes de luz em toda a região.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The storm caused power cuts across the whole region.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Originar-se} — to originate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{originar} is built on \emph{origem} \textquotedblleft{}origin\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{orīgō, orīginis} \textquotedblleft{}beginning, source\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{orīrī} \textquotedblleft{}to rise\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{originar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{originar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to derive, then the Portuguese for to result, then say \emph{originar} again

\section[graças a]{graças a — thanks to}

\label{lesson:PT-C350-gracas-a}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to result, then the Portuguese for to give rise to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: graças a}
\textbf{graças a} — \textquotedblleft{}thanks to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Graças a ti, cheguei a horas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Thanks to you, I arrived on time.}
\end{quote}

For good results; for bad ones Portuguese says \emph{por causa de}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{graças a} is built on \emph{graça} \textquotedblleft{}grace, favour\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{grātia} \textquotedblleft{}favour, gratitude, thanks\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{graças a}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{graças a}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{graças a}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to result, then the Portuguese for to give rise to, then say \emph{graças a} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does graças a mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Thanks to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Revisão dos capítulos 343–350}

\label{lesson:PT-R350-revisao-343-350}



\begin{quote}
Say the Portuguese for the misunderstanding and to clarify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the misunderstanding, to clarify, the clarification, to stress, to point out
  \item to evaluate, the judgement, to judge, objective, subjective
  \item the advantage, the disadvantage, the aspect, the criticism, to weigh up
  \item the reasoning, to deduce, to conclude, the conclusion, the criterion
  \item the controversy, controversial, to dispute, to rebut, relevant
  \item the effect, to bring about, to cause, the factor, the consequence
  \item since, given that, seeing as, consequently, due to
  \item the origin, to derive, to result, to give rise to, thanks to
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The misunderstanding? (\textbf{o equívoco}.) To clarify? (\textbf{esclarecer}.) The clarification? (\textbf{o esclarecimento}.) To stress? (\textbf{sublinhar}.) To point out? (\textbf{salientar}.) To evaluate? (\textbf{avaliar}.) The judgement? (\textbf{o juízo}.) To judge? (\textbf{julgar}.) Objective? (\textbf{objetivo}.) Subjective? (\textbf{subjetivo}.) The advantage? (\textbf{a vantagem}.) The disadvantage? (\textbf{a desvantagem}.) The aspect? (\textbf{o aspeto}.) The criticism? (\textbf{a crítica}.) To weigh up? (\textbf{ponderar}.) The reasoning? (\textbf{o raciocínio}.) To deduce? (\textbf{deduzir}.) To conclude? (\textbf{concluir}.) The conclusion? (\textbf{a conclusão}.) The criterion? (\textbf{o critério}.) The controversy? (\textbf{a polémica}.) Controversial? (\textbf{polémico}.) To dispute? (\textbf{contestar}.) To rebut? (\textbf{rebater}.) Relevant? (\textbf{relevante}.) The effect? (\textbf{o efeito}.) To bring about? (\textbf{provocar}.) To cause? (\textbf{causar}.) The factor? (\textbf{o fator}.) The consequence? (\textbf{a consequência}.) Since? (\textbf{visto que}.) Given that? (\textbf{dado que}.) Seeing as? (\textbf{uma vez que}.) Consequently? (\textbf{consequentemente}.) Due to? (\textbf{devido a}.) The origin? (\textbf{a origem}.) To derive? (\textbf{derivar}.) To result? (\textbf{resultar}.) To give rise to? (\textbf{originar}.) Thanks to? (\textbf{graças a}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
